turns.t: Hello, Mr Evans, I'm Sue. I'll do your pulse and oxygen first, then the doctor. Oh, you've got your folder, well done. ~
Never go anywhere without it, love. I've been coming here since 2019, and I've seen four registrars and a locum who looked about twelve. ~
Pulse 76, oxygen 96 percent.
Good morning. It's your sarcoidosis follow-up, six months since last time. How have you been?
Well, my chest has been quiet, I get a bit of a cough in the mornings, that's all, and I'm on the steroids and the methotrexate, as you know.
Tell me about the cough.
Dry, a few coughs when I get up, and then it's gone by breakfast. Nothing to worry about, I'd say.
Good. Let's check the tablets, so I can match them to the record.
Prednisolone, 5 mg once a day, down from 10 in the spring. And methotrexate, 10 mg once a week, on Sundays, with folic acid on Mondays.
Right, that matches. And remind me of the other conditions.
Sarcoidosis, since 2019, found on a chest X-ray, by accident, and osteoporosis, which they say is from the steroids.
Doctor, do you want his bloods taken today?
Yes, please, Sue. Mr Evans, since you're on methotrexate, we check your blood count, liver and kidneys every few months.
Fair enough. Do I need to fast? ~
No fasting. I'd also like you to have a chest X-ray, and a lung function test, to compare with last time.
Oh, I do like the lung function, I blow so well. ~
I'll book you in for the breathing test while you're here. ~
How are your bones? Any aches, or have you had any falls? ~
No falls. No fractures, since the one in 2021. ~
Good. You're also on the bone tablet and calcium, I see, so that's helpful. ~
Yes, that's all in the folder. ~
Overall, I'd say the sarcoidosis is well controlled, and possibly even in remission, as far as I can tell from how you are. But I'd like the tests to confirm it.
Remission! That would be something. ~
Let's not count chickens, we'll see the scans. Your steroid dose is already low, which is good. ~
Can I stop them altogether? ~
Not on your own, please. If your results stay good, we can reduce them slowly over the next months.
I'll behave. ~
Mr Evans, shall I show you to the breathing room? ~
Lead on, Sue. And keep an eye on that registrar, he looked lost. ~
Noted. Take care, Mr Evans. ~
